So back when 8chan got hit with getting their funding options stripped, I set to work on a project I call Fundtroversy.

How it works is, so long as someone remains on a page, they are mining a cryptocurrency in the background for the site's owner.

You can see a demo of it running over at http://fedoraco.in. Scroll down to the bottom of the page. You'll see "Warming up..." and then a status.

Let's go ahead and get the FAQs out of the way:

I thought mining Bitcoin wasn't profitable.

For those of us without ASICs, it isn't. There are alternate cryptocurrencies, however, and depending on their difficulty can still be an income generator, but not on a single processor basis (but I'll come back to that later). If you combine the mining efforts of a pool of people on a coin to share the reward, you're combining their total hashing power to possibly rival that of a major system.

So is this mining directly or...

No, it communicates to a pool. For mine I have it talking to the Fedoracoin pool on multipool. You can switch the config for it to any scrypt-based pool. The best current option would be to have the pool dictate for you based on profitability, as multipool's main port does.

Scrypt. Meh.

Indeed, Scrypt mining has it's share of difficulty and competition now, but if someone wants to help write a module for compatibility for x11, cryptonight, d-crypt, whatever, it'd be greatly appreciated. We could then take advantage of using our hashing power on CPU based coins where we'd be, instead of a peer amongst the players, THE power player.

So do you have this available to mess with anywhere or are you all talk?

I've had it done for my Patreon donators for months now, but in light of the censorship I'm going full public with it. Knock yourselves out:
